payload.verdict: Your customer success work at Northwind Analytics is easy to place, and the account portfolio gives it weight. I’d move it forward with a question: what changed after you introduced the renewal-risk reviews?
write_up: You’ve moved from logistics account coordination into B2B SaaS customer success. I read your resume for Customer Success Manager roles: the portfolio and customer leadership work are clear, but the resume says less about what happened with renewals.

The line about 32 B2B SaaS accounts and $2.4M in annual recurring revenue is the best model. It names both the work and the portfolio you managed. The objective above it could belong to almost anyone and doesn’t point to customer success.

Let’s start by replacing the objective with the job you want and the account work you’ve done. Then make the renewal-risk reviews more useful to a recruiter by adding what you did with the findings and what changed, if you can substantiate it. Trim the generic team-player language to make room.

cards.line: Results-driven, detail-oriented professional seeking a challenging role where I can utilize my skills.
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can’t tell which job you want from this. Your B2B SaaS account work is a much stronger introduction.
cards.example: Customer Success Manager with experience managing 32 B2B SaaS accounts and $2.4M in annual recurring revenue
cards.question: Is Customer Success Manager the job you want next?

cards.line: Responsible for managing customer relationships and renewals
cards.cannot_tell: This names the responsibility but not what you did to manage renewals. Your next line already covers the accounts, so use this space for the renewal work itself or trim it.
cards.example: Managed customer relationships and renewals by [renewal work]
cards.question: What did you do during the renewal process?

cards.line: Managed 32 B2B SaaS accounts with $2.4M in annual recurring revenue
cards.cannot_tell: Keep this. It puts your ownership and the value of the accounts together, so a recruiter doesn’t have to guess how much business you handled.

cards.line: Introduced monthly renewal-risk reviews across the portfolio
cards.cannot_tell: Introducing the reviews is useful work. What happened with the risks you identified is still open, and that matters for a renewal-focused role.
cards.example: Introduced monthly renewal-risk reviews across the portfolio, using the findings to [action taken]
cards.question: What did you do with the findings from the reviews?

cards.line: Team player with excellent communication skills
cards.cannot_tell: This could describe almost anyone. Give that space to customer work you can name, or trim the line.
cards.example: [Customer success work you did] with [who] to [purpose]
cards.question: What customer work could you add here instead?

cards.line: Assisted account managers with various tasks as needed
cards.cannot_tell: Assisted keeps your part appropriately modest, but the tasks could mean almost anything. Name one piece of account work that was yours.
cards.question: Which account task did you assist with?

cards.cannot_tell: The list doesn’t show which tools you used for customer success. Communication and leadership are more convincing when the jobs show them in action.
cards.example: Microsoft Office, [customer success tools used], [other relevant skills]
cards.question: Which customer success tools or relevant skills have you used that you can add?

fit.why: Your latest role manages B2B SaaS accounts, renewals and customer leadership reviews.
fit.level: mid-level, manages a B2B SaaS account portfolio
fit.note: Your experience points toward customer success roles with an account and renewal focus. The earlier logistics role adds client-facing work, while Northwind should carry the most detail.
